intro_notes: Scouts BSA Test Lab Pilot Badge (Valid through 2026-12-31). The Auctioneering Badge is a dynamic blend of public speaking and salesmanship that offers Scouts the opportunity to develop essential communication and persuasion skills. Scouts will learn about the history of auctioneering, develop presentation techniques, and build rapport with an audience. They’ll engage in mock auctions to practice creating demand and closing deals while also learning how to handle challenges and uphold ethical standards. This badge fosters confidence and critical thinking skills that are powerful tools for personal growth, leadership roles, and future success.

NOTE: Any registered adult Scouting America volunteer may serve as the counselor/reviewer for a Test Lab badge. Upon completion of all requirements and the official Scouting America Test Lab survey, Scouts receive an official Certificate of Completion that converts to Merit Badge credit if the badge graduates to permanent status.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: During a live charity auction, a bidder raises their hand to place a $100 bid, and simultaneously a collaborator in the crowd places a fake 'shill' bid solely to artificially drive up the price without intending to buy. Under the National Auctioneers Association Code of Ethics, how must the auctioneer handle shill bidding?
options: Encourage secret shill bidders in the audience so the seller gets a higher commission.
Strictly prohibit fake or shill bidding, disclose whether an item is Absolute or Reserve before bidding opens, and recognize only bona fide transparent bids.
Change the auction terms from Absolute to Reserve after the gavel falls.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Prohibit deceptive shill bidding and clearly state all terms (Absolute vs. Reserve and buyer's premium) before opening the lot.
quiz_item.explanation: Auctioneering ethics and state licensing laws require complete transparency in bid calling; undisclosed shill bidding is fraudulent and destroys buyer trust.

(C) View an online auction until the sale is concluded and discuss it with your counselor.
